title: Chapter 2: Atoms, Molecules, and Ions
content:
ሰላም የተወደዳችሁ የ EthioFresh ጀግና ተማሪዎቻችን! 👋 እንኳን ወደ ኬሚስትሪ ምዕራፍ 2 ክፍል 2 (Chapter 2: Chemical Formulas & The Periodic Table) በደስታ መጣችሁ! በዛሬው ጥልቅ ቱቶሪያላችን ስለ ኬሚካል ፎርሙላዎች (Molecular & Empirical Formulas)፣ የሞለኪዩላር ሞዴሎች፣ የአቶሞች እና ሞለኪውሎች ልዩነት፣ እንዲሁም የፔሪዮዲክ ቴብል ታሪካዊ እድገት እና የኤለመንቶች ምደባ (Metals, Nonmetals, Groups & Periods) በዝርዝር እንመለከታለን። በርቱ፣ ውጤታችንን አብረን እናበራለን!

2.2. Chemical Formulas

A molecular formula is a representation of a molecule that uses chemical symbols to indicate the types of atoms followed by subscripts to show the number of atoms of each type in the molecule. A subscript is used only when more than one atom of a given type is present. Molecular formulas are also used as abbreviations for the names of compounds.

A structural formula for a compound gives the same information as its molecular formula (the types and numbers of atoms in the molecule) but also shows how the atoms are connected in the molecule. For example, in methane (CH4), the lines represent chemical bonds that hold the atoms together.

Molecular Representations & Models

  • Molecular Formula: Shows chemical symbols and exact numbers of atoms (e.g., CH4).
  • Structural Formula: Shows chemical symbols and lines representing bonds connecting the atoms.
  • Ball-and-stick Model: Shows the geometric arrangement of the atoms with atomic sizes not to scale.
  • Space-filling Model: Shows the relative sizes of the atoms fitting closely together.

👉 የኬሚካል ፎርሙላ የአንድን ሞለኪውል ስብጥር ያሳያል። Molecular formula የትኞቹ ኤለመንቶች ስንት አቶም እንዳላቸው በ subscript (ከስር በሚጻፍ ቁጥር) ሲገልጽ፣ Structural formula ደግሞ አቶሞቹ እንዴት እንደተያያዙ በቦንድ (lines) ያሳያል። Ball-and-stick እና Space-filling ሞዴሎች ደግሞ የሞለኪውሉን ባለ 3D ጂኦሜትሪያዊ ቅርፅ እና መጠን ያሳያሉ።

Diatomic Molecules and Polyatomic Elements

Although many elements consist of discrete, individual atoms, several exist naturally as molecules made up of two or more atoms chemically bonded together:

  • Diatomic Molecules: Elements composed of molecules containing two atoms each. These seven elements are: H2, O2, N2, F2, Cl2, Br2, and I2.
  • Polyatomic Form of Sulfur: The most common form of elemental sulfur is composed of molecules containing eight sulfur atoms, written as S8.

Distinction Between Subscripts and Coefficients

It is crucial to understand that a subscript following a symbol and a number in front of a symbol represent distinctly different entities:

  • H: Represents one single atom of hydrogen.
  • 2H: Represents two separate, unbonded hydrogen atoms.
  • H2: Represents one diatomic molecule of hydrogen (two hydrogen atoms chemically bonded together).
  • 2H2: Represents two diatomic molecules of hydrogen (a total of four hydrogen atoms in two bonded pairs).

👉 በኬሚስትሪ ውስጥ 7 ኤለመንቶች (H₂, O₂, N₂, F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, I₂) በየሁለት አቶም ተጣማሪ ሆነው (Diatomic molecules) ይገኛሉ። H₂ ማለት አንድ ላይ የተያያዙ ሁለት አቶሞች (አንድ ሞለኪውል) ሲሆን፣ 2H ማለት ግን ያልተያያዙ ነጠላ ሁለት አቶሞች ማለት ነው። 2H₂ ደግሞ ሁለት የ H₂ ሞለኪውሎች (በአጠቃላይ 4 አቶሞች) ማለት ነው።

Empirical Formulas vs. Molecular Formulas

Compounds can be described using empirical formulas or molecular formulas depending on the analytical data available:

  • Empirical Formula: Indicates the types of atoms present and the simplest whole-number ratio of the number of atoms (or ions) in the compound. For example, titanium dioxide (used in paint and sunscreen) has an empirical formula of TiO2, indicating a 1:2 ratio of titanium to oxygen atoms.
  • Molecular Formula: Indicates the actual numbers of atoms of each element in a molecule of the compound.
💡 Exam Hint:
Key Relationship: A molecular formula is always a whole-number multiple of an empirical formula!
Molecular Formula = n × (Empirical Formula)
Where n is a positive integer (1, 2, 3, ...). If n = 1, the empirical formula and molecular formula are identical (e.g., H2O).

Examples of Empirical vs. Molecular Formulas

CompoundMolecular FormulaAtom RatioSimplest RatioEmpirical Formula
BenzeneC6H66 : 61 : 1CH
Acetic Acid (Vinegar)C2H4O22 : 4 : 21 : 2 : 1CH2O
Glucose (Blood Sugar)C6H12O66 : 12 : 61 : 2 : 1CH2O
Metaldehyde (Pesticide)C8H16O48 : 16 : 42 : 4 : 1C2H4O
WaterH2O2 : 12 : 1H2O

👉 Empirical formula ማለት በውህዱ (compound) ውስጥ ያሉ ኤለመንቶች የአቶሞች ቁጥር አነስተኛው ሙሉ ቁጥር ሬሺዮ (simplest whole-number ratio) ነው። Molecular formula ደግሞ በሞለኪውሉ ውስጥ በርግጥ የሚገኘውን ትክክለኛ የአቶሞች ቁጥር ያሳያል። ለምሳሌ Benzene (C₆H₆) ወደ አነስተኛ ሬሺዮ ሲቀየር CH ይሆናል።

Worked Examples: Empirical and Molecular Formulas

Example 2.4: Empirical and Molecular Formulas of Glucose

Problem: Molecules of glucose (blood sugar) contain 6 carbon atoms, 12 hydrogen atoms, and 6 oxygen atoms. What are the molecular and empirical formulas of glucose?

Solution Step-by-Step:
• Molecular Formula: Write the symbols with subscripts representing the actual counts → C6H12O6.
• Ratio Analysis: The ratio of C to H to O atoms is 6 : 12 : 6.
• Simplest Ratio: Divide each subscript by the greatest common divisor (6):
  6/6 = 1, 12/6 = 2, 6/6 = 1 → Ratio is 1 : 2 : 1.
• Empirical Formula: CH2O.

Check Your Learning (Exercise: Metaldehyde):

Problem: A molecule of metaldehyde (a pesticide used for snails and slugs) contains 8 carbon atoms, 16 hydrogen atoms, and 4 oxygen atoms. What are the molecular and empirical formulas of metaldehyde?

Solution Step-by-Step:
• Molecular Formula: C8H16O4.
• Ratio Analysis: Ratio of C : H : O = 8 : 16 : 4.
• Simplest Ratio: Divide all subscripts by the greatest common divisor (4):
  8/4 = 2, 16/4 = 4, 4/4 = 1 → Ratio is 2 : 4 : 1.
• Empirical Formula: C2H4O.

2.3. The Periodic Table

2.3.1. Historical Development of the Periodic Table

As early chemists purified ores and discovered elements, they recognized that certain elements could be grouped together based on similar chemical behaviors:

  • Group 1 Behavior: Lithium (Li), Sodium (Na), and Potassium (K) are shiny, conduct heat and electricity, and form compounds with oxygen in a 2:1 atom ratio (e.g., Li2O).
  • Group 2 Behavior: Calcium (Ca), Strontium (Sr), and Barium (Ba) are shiny, good conductors, and form compounds with oxygen in a 1:1 atom ratio (e.g., CaO).
  • Halogen Behavior: Fluorine (F), Chlorine (Cl), Bromine (Br), and Iodine (I) exhibit distinct reactive properties similar to one another.

Mendeleev and Meyer vs. Modern Periodic Law

In 1869, Dimitri Mendeleev in Russia and Lothar Meyer in Germany independently recognized a periodic relationship among elemental properties. Both published periodic tables with elements arranged according to increasing atomic mass.

  • Mendeleev's Genius: Mendeleev used his table to predict the existence of elements with properties similar to aluminum and silicon that were yet unknown.
  • Validation: The subsequent discoveries of Gallium (1875) and Germanium (1886) matched Mendeleev's predictions remarkably well, solidifying acceptance of his periodic table (which initially contained 8 groups and 12 periods).
  • The Modern Periodic Law: By the 20th century, it became clear that periodic relationships depend on atomic numbers (Z) rather than atomic masses.
    Periodic Law: The properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

👉 የመጀመሪያውን የፔሪዮዲክ ቴብል ድሚትሪ መንደሌቭ (Dimitri Mendeleev) በ1869 አዘጋጀ። እሱ ኤለመንቶችን በ Atomic Mass ቅደም ተከተል ያደራጀ ሲሆን ያልተገኙ ኤለመንቶችን (ለምሳሌ Gallium እና Germanium) አስቀድሞ በመተንበዩ ይታወቃል። ነገር ግን የዘመናዊው ፔሪዮዲክ ቴብል ህግ (Modern Periodic Law) የሚያስረዳው የኤለመንቶች ባህሪ የሚወሰነው በ Atomic Number (የፕሮቶን ቁጥር) እንጂ በ Atomic Mass አለመሆኑን ነው።

2.3.2. Classification of Elements in the Periodic Table

The modern periodic table arranges elements in increasing order of atomic numbers and groups atoms with similar properties in the same vertical column.

  • Periods: 7 horizontal rows labeled 1 through 7.
  • Groups (Families): 18 vertical columns labeled 1 through 18 (recommended by IUPAC).

Three Major Classes of Elements

ClassPhysical & Chemical PropertiesLocation on Periodic TableExamples
MetalsShiny, malleable (deformed without breaking), ductile (drawn into wires), good conductors of heat & electricity.Center and left-hand sideNa, Mg, Fe, Cu, Au
NonmetalsDull appearance, brittle solids, poor conductors of heat & electricity.Upper right-hand sideC, N, O, F, Cl, Ne
Metalloids (Semimetals)Conduct heat & electricity moderately well; possess intermediate properties of both metals & nonmetals.Along the dividing line ("staircase")B, Si, Ge, As, Sb, Te

Regions and Specific Group Names

  • Main-Group Elements (Representative Elements): Columns 1, 2, and 13 through 18.
  • Transition Metals: Columns 3 through 12.
  • Inner Transition Metals: Two rows at the bottom of the table:
    • Lanthanides: Top row of inner transition metals.
    • Actinides: Bottom row of inner transition metals.

Special Group Names (Families)

  • Group 1 (Alkali Metals): Highly reactive metals (except Hydrogen). Form 1+ cations.
  • Group 2 (Alkaline Earth Metals): Reactive metals. Form 2+ cations.
  • Group 15 (Pnictogens): Nitrogen family.
  • Group 16 (Chalcogens / Oxygen Family): Oxygen family.
  • Group 17 (Halogens): Highly reactive nonmetals. Form 1- anions.
  • Group 18 (Noble Gases / Inert Gases): Very unreactive, stable monoatomic nonmetals.
  • Hydrogen (H): A unique nonmetallic element with properties similar to both Group 1 and Group 17 elements. Positioned at the top of Group 1 or on its own.

👉 ፔሪዮዲክ ቴብል 7 አግድም ረድፎች (Periods) እና 18 ቀጥተኛ አምዶች (Groups) አሉት። ኤለመንቶች በሶስት ዋና ዋና ክፍሎች ይከፈላቸዋል፦ Metals (አብረቅራቂ እና ኮንዳክተር)፣ Nonmetals (ደማቅ ያልሆኑ እና ባልደረባ) እና Metalloids (የሁለቱም ባህሪ ያላቸው)። በተጨማሪም Group 1 (Alkali metals)፣ Group 2 (Alkaline earth metals)፣ Group 15 (Pnictogens)፣ Group 16 (Chalcogens)፣ Group 17 (Halogens) እና Group 18 (Noble gases) በመባል ይታወቃሉ።

Worked Examples: Group Classification

Example 2.5: Naming Groups of Elements

Problem: Atoms of each of the following elements are essential for life. Give the group name for the following elements:
(a) Chlorine      (b) Calcium      (c) Sodium

Solution Step-by-Step:
• (a) Chlorine (Cl): Located in Group 17 → Halogen.
• (b) Calcium (Ca): Located in Group 2 → Alkaline earth metal.
• (c) Sodium (Na): Located in Group 1 → Alkali metal.

Check Your Learning (Group Names Exercise):

Problem: Give the group name for each of the following elements:
(a) Nitrogen      (b) Oxygen      (c) Argon      (d) Barium

Solution Step-by-Step:
• (a) Nitrogen (N): Located in Group 15 → Pnictogen.
• (b) Oxygen (O): Located in Group 16 → Chalcogen (or Oxygen family).
• (c) Argon (Ar): Located in Group 18 → Noble gas (Inert gas).
• (d) Barium (Ba): Located in Group 2 → Alkaline earth metal.
